subject: AcreetionOS Update — July 18, 2026
body:
The AcreetionOS continuous integration pipeline has been further refined with the addition of per-pipeline staging directories and relative symlinks for the latest.iso file, making our ISO build process more reliable and efficient. This enhancement is a testament to our community's dedication to improving the workflow and ensuring that users receive the most up-to-date and stable versions of AcreetionOS, which can be found on our website at https://acreetionos.org/.

Development
The recent updates to our CI pipeline have been instrumental in streamlining our build process, and we're seeing positive results from these changes. As we continue to work on refining our workflow, we're also keeping a close eye on the latest developments in the Linux ecosystem, including the recent release of Emacs 31.1 and the latest stable kernel set, which can be found in the Arch repos.

Community
Our community has been actively engaged in discussions around security updates, with recent updates issued for various packages, including ansible-core, cups-filters, and curl. We encourage all users to stay up-to-date with the latest security patches and to report any issues they may encounter. For more information on our community efforts, please visit our wiki at https://acreetionos.org/wiki.html, and to stay current with our latest developments, check out our changelog at https://acreetionos.org/changelog.html.

Tip of the day
For users looking to get the most out of AcreetionOS, we recommend checking out our documentation at https://acreetionos.org/docs.html, which provides detailed guides on how to use our immutable-style workflow and take advantage of our simple and efficient design. Additionally, our flash page at https://acreetionos.org/flash.html offers a quick overview of our project's goals and features.
